pairs.why: A has clean, simple edges on the posts and planks with little going on in the background, like the real card's smooth forms. B fills the water with a dense net of crisp caustic lines that adds a lot of background edges.
A's panel seams are thin and soft and the ball's outer edge is gently modulated like the real ball. B's seams look slightly firmer and darker.
B softens the background so the hero holds the sharpest edges, as on the real card. A has crisp railing bolts, bench and base rivets, so it has many edges in the background and in the hero.
A's body edges are softer, with no dark contour lines. B's rim highlight and key edges are a little crisper than the real card's soft bevels.
B's canopy panels blend more softly with fewer dark contour lines. A has crisp scalloped edges with darker lines between panels.
B has a soft, simplified background and smooth, thin body seams, as on the real card. A's window, curtain and props add many crisp background edges and a glowing hard stripe.
A is a thick rope with soft, rounded edges and gently blended strand lines, like the real cards' puffy forms. B's thin rope has crisp fine twist lines and more edges.
Both ropes are thin with similarly crisp twist lines and a crisp outer edge. Edges and linework give no reason to choose.
